title: Subhash Singhal @ Banti Chaudhary vs Ashwani Gupta on 24 February, 2025
full_text: Subhash Singhal @ Banti Chaudhary vs Ashwani Gupta on 24 February, 2025 IN THE COURT OF SH. VINOD KUMAR, JUDICIAL MAGISTRATE FIRST CLASS (NI ACT-04), SAKET COURTS, NEW DELHI CNR No. DLST020189562023 IN THE MATTER OF: CC NI ACT 7593/2023 SUBHASH SINGHAL @ BANTI CHAUDHARY Vs. ASHWANI GUPTA 1. Complainant Case Number : CC NI ACT 7593/2023 2. Name of the Complainant : Subhash Singhal @ Banty Chaudhary, S/o Sh. S.P Singhal, R/o H.No. A-164, Raju Park, Khanpur, New Delhi-110080 3. Name and address of the : Ashwani Gupta, accused S/o Late Sh. Davender Gupta, R/o Shop No. 8, DDA Market, J.J. Colony, Near Post Office, Dispensary, Khanpur, New Delhi-110080 4. Offence complained proved : Under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 5. Plea of the accused : Pleaded not guilty 6. Final Order : Acquitted 7. Date of Institution : 16.09.2023 8. Date on which reserved for : 04.02.2025 Judgment 9. Date of Judgement : 24.02.2025 COMPLAINT UNDER SECTION 138 NEGOTIABLE INSTRUMENTS ACT, 1881. JUDGMENT CC NI ACT 7593/2023 SUBHASH SINGHAL @ BANTI CHAUDHARY Vs. ASHWANI GUPTA PAGE NO. 1/12 Digitally signed by VINOD VINOD KUMAR Date: KUMAR 2025.02.24 17:21:38 +0530 1. By way of this judgment, this court shall dispose of the present complaint ﬁled by Sh. Subhash Singhal @ Banty Chaudhary (hereinafter referred to as 'complainant') against Ashwani Gupta (hereinafter referred to as 'accused') u/s 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (hereinafter referred to as ' NI Act ' in short. BRIEF FACTS 2. It is the case of the complainant that in the month of July, 2016, the accused was in urgent need of money and therefore, approached the complainant for financial assistance to the extent of Rs. 6,00,000/- on the promise that the amount shall be reimbursed within one year. It is further stated by the complainant that the complaint being know to the accused and seeing the urgency of the accused, the complainant advanced a loan of Rs. 6,00,000/- in the month of July, 2016 under the impression that the abovesaid loan amount would be returned within one year. It is further alleged by the complainant that the accused issued a cheque bearing No. 236224 dated 10.06.2023 in favor of the Complainant for a sum of Rs. 6,00,000/- (hereinafter referred to as the "Cheque in question") and when the complainant presented the aforesaid cheque for presentation, the same was returned unpaid with the remarks "funds insufficient" vide return memo dated 27.07.2023. It is further stated that thereafter, within the stipulated time, the complainant sent a legal demand notice dated 01.08.2023 calling upon the accused to pay the total outstanding amount of Rs. 6,00,000/-, but despite service of legal demand notice to the accused, he has not made any payment to the Complainant till date against the said liability. PROCEEDINGS BEFORE THE COURT 3. The cognizance of the complaint was taken and prima facie the oﬀence u/s 138 NI Act was made out against accused who was summoned vide order dated 21.09.2023. The notice u/s 251 of Cr.P.C. CC NI ACT 7593/2023 SUBHASH SINGHAL @ BANTI CHAUDHARY Vs. ASHWANI GUPTA PAGE NO. 2/12 Digitally signed by VINOD VINOD KUMAR Date: KUMAR 2025.02.24 17:21:44 +0530 was served upon the accused on 04.11.2023 to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Thereafter, oral application of accused u/s. 145(2) of NI Act was allowed and the complainant was examined, cross- examined and discharged. Statement of accused u/s 313 of Cr.P.C was recorded on 08.04.2024 in which the accused chose to lead defence evidence and subsequently, examined himself as defence witness who was duly cross examined by the complainant. Therefore, D.E. was closed on 25.06.2024 and the matter was listed for ﬁnal arguments. After this, final arguments were advanced by the parties and written arguments were also filed on behalf of the accused. EVIDENCE 4. In order to prove his case, the complainant had examined himself as CW-1 by way of affidavit CW-1/A and relied upon the following documents: Ex.CW-1/1 Cheque bearing no. 236224 dated 10.06.2023 for an amount of Rs. 6,00,000/- drawn on Canara Bank, Saket Branch, New Delhi Ex.CW-1/2 Bank Return Memo dated 27.07.2023 Ex.CW-1/3 Legal demand notice dated 01.08.2023 Ex.CW-1/4 Postal receipt qua legal demand notice. Ex.CW-1/5 Tracking report of delivery of legal demand notice. Ex.CW-1/6 Delivery of legal demand notice through Whatsapp Ex.CW-1/6 (i) Affidavit under Section 65B, Indian Evidence act in support of legal demand notice to accused through Whatsapp Ex.CW-1/A Evidence by way of affidavit Digitally signed VINOD by VINOD KUMAR KUMAR Date: 2025.02.24 17:21:51 +0530 CC NI ACT 7593/2023 SUBHASH SINGHAL @ BANTI CHAUDHARY Vs. ASHWANI GUPTA PAGE NO. 3/12 ARGUMENTS ADVANCED 5. Ld. Counsel for the complainant argued that there exists legally enforceable liability in favour of the complainant on the basis of presumption under section 139 NI Act read with Section 118(a) of the NI Act and also on the basis of the averments made in the complaint, the evidence by way of affidavit and documents relied upon by the complainant. It was contended that the accused has not disputed the genuineness and signatures on the cheque in the notice framed u/s. 251 Cr.P.C rather he has admitted that the signatures on the cheque were his. It was lastly argued that all the essential ingredients u/s. 138 of NI Act stand fulfilled and the accused should be convicted. 6. Per contra, Ld. Counsel for accused argues that Section 138 of the NI Act is not attracted as there was no legally enforceable debt because at no point of time any loan was borrowed from the complainant by the Accused. He further argues that no legal demand notice was ever received to the accused because the complainant deliberately dispatched the registered legal demand notice on wrong addressee i.e Shop No-8, DDA Market, JJ Colony, Near Post Office, Dispensary, Khanpur, New Delhi-110080 instead of Shop No-8, First Floor, DDA Market, JJ Colony, Khanpur, New Delhi- 110062. It is further argued that as claimed by the Complainant that What's App message of the demand notice was served upon two Mobile Nos. ie. 9650785711 & 9971923867, however Accused having One mobile No-9560785711 and his wife number is 9999243767 and admittedly no legal demand notice was dispatched by the Complainant on these numbers, hence the basic ingredient of Section 138 N.I. Act is missing and is relying on Judgments of the Hon' ble Supreme Court in " M.D Thomas Vs P.S. Jaleel " (2009 (14) SCC-398) & Hon'ble Gujarat High Court in " Patel Amrutbhai Narayandas Vs State of Gujarat " (2012 (2) DCR-74). He CC NI ACT 7593/2023 SUBHASH SINGHAL @ BANTI CHAUDHARY Vs. ASHWANI GUPTA PAGE NO. 4/12 Digitally signed by VINOD VINOD KUMAR Date: KUMAR 2025.02.24 17:22:25 +0530 submits that the notices dispatched to the Accused No-1 has been returned with the remark " No Such Person in the address", however as per Para No-5" as per Postal report states that the postman found the door of the house locked on frequent visit.". He further argues that the demand notice U/s 138(b) NI Act was not served upon accused, and even if received by any of family members, does not tantamount to compliance of provision. 7. Ld. Counsel for accused has further relied upon the Judgment in " Anil Raj Vs Integrated Finance Co. Ltd " 2006 (1) ALD Cri 36 , it was held Notice sent to the Petitioner was returned to the sender with the endorsement 'Addressee left India. He argues that in these circumstances, the Petitioner's case is that postal endorsement & the passport details would be sufficient to hold that there was no notice to him as contemplated by the Act. 8. Ld. Counsel for accused submits that the cheque in question was mis-utilized by the complainant as the cheque in question along with other documents were lost and in respect of theses cheques and documents, the NCR was lodged by the accused and his family members time to time, which is already Ex.CW-1/D1 & Ex.CW-1/D2. 9. He further submits that the accused was suffering from obesity issue since 2016 due to his weight problem of 227 Kg and he was unable to move from his house, so the question of visiting the complainant office and obtaining loan from him did not substantiate. He submits that in this regard, the medical documents were brought on record which is already Ex.DW1/2 and Ex.DW1/3. 10. Ld. Counsel for the accused argues that the complainant failed to annex any single document along with the complaint such as bank statement as well as his Income Tax returns & Balance Sheet etc were filed by the complainant, however during the cross examination only ITR for the CC NI ACT 7593/2023 SUBHASH SINGHAL @ BANTI CHAUDHARY Vs. ASHWANI GUPTA PAGE NO. 5/12 Digitally signed by VINOD VINOD KUMAR Date: KUMAR 2025.02.24 17:22:31 +0530 FY-2016-17 was brought, which indicate his total Income of Rs. 3,22,000/- and Sundry debtor show the total amount of Rs.1,50,000/-, However he claimed that alleged sum of Rs. 6,00,000/- stated to have been lend to the Accused was not reflected in the ITR of the complainant. Ld. Counsel for accused argues that the complainant failed to bring his Bank statement to reflect / reveal his financial capacity of the Complainant and the complainant claimed that he had paid sum of Rs. 6 lakh in cash and did not obtain any receipt of aforesaid loan amount from the Accused. 11. Ld. Counsel for accused has argued that accused neither received any alleged loan from the complainant nor the complainant has proved the same beyond reasonable doubt that the Accused had borrowed the said amount, moreover, unaccounted huge cash amount of Rs. 6 Lakh is barred U/s 269 SS of the Income Tax Act and hence provision of Section 138 cannot be resorted to for recovery of an unaccounted amount. Ld. Counsel has further relied upon the Judgment in " Sanjay Mishra Vs Kanishka Kapoor " held by Hon'ble Bombay High Court 2009(2) DCR-244 and in " Rajaram Vs Maruthachalam " (2023 LiveLaw(SC) 46) recently passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held that adjudication in Criminal cases is based on the principal that the accused is presumed to be innocent and the guilt of the accused should be proved to the hilt and the proof should be beyond all reasonable doubt. Ld. Counsel for accused argues that the accused has successfully rebutted both the presumption under Section 118 & 139 of NIA. APPRECIATION OF EVIDENCE 12. It is pertinent to mention that to establish the offence under Section 138 of the NI Act against the accused, the complainant must prove the following ingredients reiterated in the Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Kusum Ingots and Alloys v. Pennar Peterson Securities Ltd . CC NI ACT 7593/2023 SUBHASH SINGHAL @ BANTI CHAUDHARY Vs. ASHWANI GUPTA PAGE NO. 6/12 Digitally signed by VINOD VINOD KUMAR KUMAR Date: 2025.02.24 17:22:37 +0530 AIR 2000 SC954:- (i) a person must have drawn a cheque on an account maintained by him in a bank for payment of a certain amount of money to another person from out of that account for the discharge of any debt or other liability; (ii) that cheque has been presented to the bank within a period of three months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of its validity whichever is earlier; (iii) that cheque is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of the account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with the bank; (iv) the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice in writing, to the drawer of the cheque, within 15 days of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid; (v) the drawer of such cheque fails to make payment of the said amount of money to the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque within 15 days of the receipt of the said notice; 13. It is pertinent to mention here that a negotiable instrument including a cheque carries presumption of consideration in terms of Section 118(a) and under Section 139 of the Act. Section 118 (a) of Negotiable Instruments Act reads as under:- "That every negotiable instrument was made or drawn for consideration and that every such instrument when it has been accepted, endorsed, negotiated or transferred was accepted, endorsed, negotiated or transferred for consideration". Section 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act reads as under:- CC NI ACT 7593/2023 SUBHASH SINGHAL @ BANTI CHAUDHARY Vs. ASHWANI GUPTA PAGE NO. 7/12 Digitally signed by VINOD VINOD KUMAR KUMAR Date: 2025.02.24 17:22:43 +0530 "It shall be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that the holder of a cheque received the cheque, of the nature referred to in section 138 , for the discharge, in whole or in part, or any debt or other liability." 14. The combined effect of Section 118(a) and Section 139 of NI Act is that it raises a presumption in favour of the holder of the cheque that he has received the same for discharge in whole or in part of any debt or other liability. The principles pertaining to the presumptions and the onus of proof were summarized by the Hon'ble Apex Court in In Jugesh Sehgal vs. Shamsher Devender Singh Vs. Deepak Madan Singh Gogi , (2009) 14 SCC 683 as under: "14. Before moving forward with the contentions of the accused, it is pertinent to note that as per the provisions of section 118(a) and Devender Singh Vs. Deepak Madan 139 of the NI Act , in every case u/s. 138 of NI Act , there is a presumption of law that the cheque has been issued for consideration and in discharge of legally enforceable debt or liability. 15. It is further pertinent to mention the relevant judgments on the point of presumption of existence of legally enforceable debt or liability. Reliance is placed by this court upon the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Rangappa v. Sri Mohan , ( 2010) 11 SCC 441, Kumar Exports vs. Sharma Carpets , ( 2009) 2 SCC 513, and Bir Singh vs. Mukesh Kumar , (2019) 4 SCC 197, wherein it has been held that the presumption u/s. 139 NI Act is a presumption of law and not presumption of fact. It has further been held that it is not necessary that the cheque must have been filled by the accused himself and the accused may be liable even when the cheque has been filled by the complainant. The essential requirement is that the liability must exist on the date of the presentation of the cheque in question. It has been further held that once the signatures on the CC NI ACT 7593/2023 SUBHASH SINGHAL @ BANTI CHAUDHARY Vs. ASHWANI GUPTA PAGE NO. 8/12 Digitally signed by VINOD VINOD KUMAR Date: KUMAR 2025.02.24 17:22:49 +0530 cheque are admitted then the court is bound to raise presumption u/s. 118 r/w. 139 NI Act regarding existence of legally enforceable debt or liability." 15. In the present matter the accused vide notice u/s. 251 Cr.P.C. has admitted his signature on the cheque, As per the scheme of the NI Act , once the accused admits signature on the cheques in question, the presumptions under Section 118(a) read with Section 139 NI Act are raised in favour of the complainant that the cheque in question was issued by the accused to the complainant in discharge of legally enforceable debt or liability and these being the rebuttable presumptions, it is now on the accused to raise a probable defence and to prove his case on the basis of preponderance of probabilities. Now, the defense taken by the accused to rebut the presumptions available in the favor of the complainant will be looked into and decided upon. FIRST DEFENCE 16. First defence raised by the accused is that the complainant has failed to send legal demand notice to the accused as per the stipulations of Section 138 NI Act and the legal demand notice sent by the complainant was never received by the accused as the same was deliberately sent by the complainant on the wrong address of the accused. Perusal of records show that the legal demand notice in the instant case was sent by the complainant through post as well as on two phone numbers of the accused through whatsapp. It has been admitted by the accused that one of these two phone numbers belong to his wife. Necessary acknowledgement qua the service of legal demand notice through whatasapp and certificate under Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 also placed on the record by the complainant. In these circumstances, the service of the legal demand notice upon the accused is deemed to have been duly effected. CC NI ACT 7593/2023 SUBHASH SINGHAL @ BANTI CHAUDHARY Vs. ASHWANI GUPTA PAGE NO. 9/12 Digitally signed by VINOD VINOD KUMAR KUMAR Date: 2025.02.24 17:22:58 +0530 SECOND DEFENCE 17. Second defence raised by the accused is that complainant has failed to prove the source of cash amount of alleged loan of Rs.4,00,000/-. Perusal of records show that demonetisation in India was declared on 08.11.2016 and the factum of alleged loan transaction stated to have occurred on 20.09.2017 i.e. after a long period of almost 10 months. In such period of time, the contention of the complaint that he arranged for the aforesaid amount of cash out of his personal savings, bank account and friends and relatives, cannot be rejected. Moreover, the accused has not discredited the testimony of complainant to that extent as no questions have been asked regarding the relevant documents such as bank transactions, ITRs etc to prove the source of cash. THIRD DEFENCE 18. Third defence raised by the accused is that the accused had lost some cheques including the cheque in question and necessary NCR qua the same was also lodged by him. However, perusal of aforesaid NCRs reflect that it does not clearly show as to regarding which cheques the said NCRs came to be registered. Further, it is contention of the accused that the cheque might have been misused by the complainant but in his examination before the Court, the accused has failed to put forth the manner in which the said cheque came to be misused by the Complainant. In view of the same, a doubt is raised on the credibility of the version of the accused. TIME BARRED DEBT 19. Perusal of record show that the alleged cheque is dated 10.06.2023 whereas the aforesaid alleged loan is said to have been advanced in July, 2016 . Therefore the debt is time barred as the same has been issued after a lapse of more than three years. In various judicial pronouncements such as Girdhari Lal Rathi Vs P.T.V Ramanujachari (1997(1)ALT(CRI)509) and CC NI ACT 7593/2023 SUBHASH SINGHAL @ BANTI CHAUDHARY Vs. ASHWANI GUPTA PAGE NO. 10/12 Digitally signed by VINOD VINOD KUMAR KUMAR Date: 2025.02.24 17:23:03 +0530 Sasseriyil Joseph Vs Devassia (2001CRILJ24 ), it is held that the cheque issued towards time barred debt will not attract the offense punishable U/s.138 of N.I. Act . It is the well settled principle of law that once a cheque is issued, even in respect of a time barred debt, the same would constitute a promise in writing as per Section 25(3) of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 and a new agreement would come into existence in terms of the said provision of Contract Act and the debt would not become time barred, unless otherwise proved by evidence to this effect. 20. Now it is for this Court to consider whether the cheque in question is issued towards time barred debt or not. In cross examination of the Complainant, it has been admitted by the complainant that the alleged cheque was issued by mother of the accused and accused while borrowing of the loan during the year 2016 and cheque is dated 10.06.2023 which is after lapse of three years. then prima facie it could be said to be an acknowledgment of the debt. FINAL ORDER 21. Therefore, in view of the discussion above, this Court is of considered view that the complainant has failed to bring his case within the period of limitation and the alleged debt being claimed by the complainant is a time-barred debt. 22. Accordingly, in light of the above discussion, the accused Ashwini Gupta stands acquitted of the offence under Section 138 of NI Act. 23. The bail bonds, if any furnished by accused at the time of commencement of trial stands canceled. Surety, if any stands discharged. Documents, if any shall be returned to its rightful owner as per rules. Endorsement, if any stands canceled. Case property, shall be disposed off after expiration of period to assail this judgment and in case of appeal, as CC NI ACT 7593/2023 SUBHASH SINGHAL @ BANTI CHAUDHARY Vs. Case file be consigned to record room after due compliance. 24. Let a signed copy of the Judgment be supplied to the accused, free of cost, and a copy of the same be placed on record.
